conflicts.quote: The strip renders eight cells at every state; an unavailable metric is an `unavailable` cell, not a missing one.
conflicts.why: SELF-REVISION. I withdraw this for the off-exchange cell. ux's CI-6 is right and I could not defend mine against it: per `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` §5 the off-exchange object is omitted both when `INCLUDE_DARK_POOL=false` and when the best-effort computation fails, and both arrive at the FE as an absent object. My rule forces that cell to render `unavailable`, which asserts an attempt was made and failed — a claim the wire cannot support and the `apps/api` diff must stay empty this phase, so no discriminator can be added. That is `[absent-is-not-none]` inverted: I would be manufacturing a reason. The cost of withdrawing is real (ux risk 5: a rail whose cardinality varies makes an off-screen cell indistinguishable from an absent one), so I am not withdrawing silently.
conflicts.proposal: The rule holds for seven of the eight cells: opportunity, net DEX, IV/HV, IV rank, vol/OI, IV skew and term structure each render a vocabulary member and keep their slot. The off-exchange cell is the declared exception — absent when the object is absent — and the strip's cardinality is therefore 7-or-8, stated in SPEC with the reason, not silently variable. The wire-level attempted/failed discriminator is booked as named debt with a phase attached, per ux CI-6.

conflicts.quote: **Required:** on a drop, that cell shows the structure flip labelled `Gamma flip` with its structure caption (distance line + as-of), or the bare-offline arm — never `last known`.
conflicts.why: The diagnosis is correct and I accept it (see `agree`), but the prescription is written against pre-latch code and, applied literally after the latch lands, deletes ruling 2's arm A for the one `LiveTape` cell that can genuinely retain a value. Ruling 2 makes the latch this phase's debt: once a last-non-null latch exists, the gamma-flip cell on a drop HAS a real retained stream value — the last live-recomputed flip — and the honest render of that is 50% opacity + pause mark + `offline · last known`. A blanket 'never `last known`' on that cell forbids the correct post-latch render. Worse, the substitute ux prescribes introduces a third fabrication shape: `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` §3 and ux's own CI-4 establish that the structure flip and the live-recomputed flip are legitimately different numbers, so swapping the structure flip in under a cell labelled `Gamma flip · live` shows the trader a different measurement under the live label at the exact moment the stream died.
conflicts.proposal: Split the requirement by latch state, which is the same two arms ruling 2 already names. Pre-latch (today's defect): `:190`'s `retained: flipValue != null` is wrong and must go — no `last known` over a bundle fallback. Post-latch (this phase's ship state): `:96`'s `?? m.gamma_flip` fallback is removed from the RETAINED computation, `retained` is keyed on the latched last-non-null STREAM flip only, and `last known` renders exactly when that latch is non-empty and never otherwise. The cell keeps its `Gamma flip · live` label with ux's CI-4 sub-copy naming the structure flip it differs from. Arm B (latch empty — no stream flip ever arrived this symbol view) renders the bare vocabulary member with the pause mark and no `last known` words, which is the render ux is actually protecting.

conflicts.quote: | A6 | cooldown / daily cap | body | A1–A4, A7–A8 | disabled control naming the wait in Mono + the cap footnote; last read still pinned |
conflicts.why: A6 folds two shipped, independently-produced states into one render case with one marker. `presentationPolicy.ts:16-17` declares `cooldown` and `daily_cap` as two distinct members of `AiRecRequestState`, and `ai-rec/copy.ts` already ships non-synonymous copy for each — `cooldownLabel` at `:167` (`Cooling down · {remaining}s`) and `capTitle` at `:169` (`Daily AI limit reached — resets {when}`), plus `retryInCooldown` at `:186` versus `retryWhenReset` at `:187`. Under ux's own UX-28 the test asserts each of the nine RENDER CASES renders its own marker, and UX-34 explicitly delegates the distinctness to UX-28 ('the distinctness itself is UX-28's test'). If cooldown and cap are one case, nothing tests that they differ — a build that renders a capped user a countdown passes the whole ux set. That directly contradicts pm's AC-50, which requires them non-synonymous and ship-adjacent, and it is the ruling-3 collapse shape at a smaller scale: a shipped distinction disappearing into a presentational union.
conflicts.proposal: Keep ux's three-axis composition model — it is right and I adopt it — but split A6 into A6a `cooldown` and A6b `daily_cap`, each with its own marker keyed on the shipped copy constants, and let the canon-16 'nine' be nine NAMES rather than nine cases. The mapping stays total via my §2.5 mechanism: one `(requestState, resultState) -> ReadLayout` function with a `never` default arm, so the split costs one union member and no new test idiom.

conflicts.quote: `containerName: 'panel'` (the phase-1 mechanism handed to R4) is applied to the hero, the strip and the AI panel, so `FigureCell`'s existing 20 → 17 → 15 container steps work inside a rail without me specifying a second sizing rule.
conflicts.why: Applying `containerName: 'panel'` AT the strip is the specific way the container ladder dies on the strip, and it fails silently at desktop. `FigureCell.tsx:216-217` queries `theme.containerQueries('panel').down(360)` and `.down(280)`; CSS resolves `@container panel` against the NEAREST ancestor bearing that name. `Widget.tsx:163` and `PanelContainer.tsx:16-17` are the only two declarations of that name in the app (verified this round). If the strip is one `Widget`, the nearest named ancestor of all eight cells is the panel body — roughly 1280px at desktop — so every cell renders at the 20px base and none ever steps to 17 or 15, at any viewport. The strip's own width is never the queried width. This is not a second sizing rule; it is the same rule resolving against the wrong box.
conflicts.proposal: Declare the name at the CELL, not the strip: wrap each strip cell in the shipped `PanelContainer` (same name, nested — the nearest-ancestor rule does the work, no new axis, no edit to `FigureCell`'s query or to `type-floor.spec.tsx`'s AC-20a assertion). The same correction applies to ux's bottom sheet, which MUI portals to `document.body` and which therefore severs container ancestry unless its root re-declares the name. `[lane-check]` stands from my R1: jsdom does not evaluate container queries, so a unit test can assert the DECLARATION only — the stepping behaviour is provable in the browser layer at a real width, never in the unit suite.

conflicts.quote: On a drop, every static figure, the field, the ladder's four structure rows and the whole quiet band are byte-identical and un-dimmed
conflicts.why: Two problems, both about the word 'field'. (a) It contradicts ux's own UX-42 and H3: the field's drift must STOP on a drop, so the field is by design not identical across a drop. A build satisfying UX-42 red-builds UX-11 and vice versa. (b) 'byte-identical' is unobservable for the field by any shipped harness. `StructureFieldCanvas.tsx` paints to a Canvas2D context and the directory contains zero `aria-`, `role=` or visually-hidden text (grepped this round, no matches); `live-dot-census.spec.tsx:171` counts DOM nodes and `single-motion-moment.spec.ts:54-55` scans for literal `@keyframes` names, so neither can see a canvas pixel. An AC nobody can run is the phase-1 GATE-Q shape wearing the phase-1 GATE-Q label.
conflicts.proposal: Scope the byte-identical clause to what has DOM text — the strip's static cells, the ladder's four structure rows, and the quiet band — where a text-content assertion is real and cheap. State the field's obligation separately and in its own terms: on a drop the curve, the wall lines and the flip line keep their last computed geometry and are not dimmed, while trail, drift, beam and sweep stop. Prove that with my §1 mechanism (extract the paint step into a pure function of `(model, ctx, now, reduced)` and drive it against a recording fake 2D context: `live: false` -> zero trail points, zero particle `arc()` calls, zero sweep gradient fills, non-zero level strokes), because that is the only mechanism on the table that can observe the canvas at all.

conflicts.quote: A null level keeps its row, renders the closed literal in Sans with no distance value, and never renders `$—`
conflicts.why: The first and third clauses are right; the middle one leaves a hole in a column. 'No distance value' means an empty cell in the distance column, and an empty cell in a column is indistinguishable from a render bug — the failure `[absent-is-not-none]` exists to name. ux's own CI-9 already accepts that an absent distance gets a literal, not a blank: it requires the MID row's distance cell to render `—`. The two rows are then treated inconsistently — the mid row's absent distance is typed, the null level's absent distance is blank — with no mechanism distinguishing them.
conflicts.proposal: The null level's distance cell renders the same not-applicable member the mid row uses (`—`), for the same reason: the distance is undefined because the level is, not because the computation failed. `distanceToLevel.ts:24-25` already returns `null` when either input is missing, so this is a caller choice at the ladder, not a change to the helper. No tenth member is requested; rule 24's closure at nine holds.

conflicts.quote: At 393, 834, 900 and 1280 in both schemes, the desk has no horizontal page overflow.
conflicts.why: The shipped suite does not run three of those eight combinations, and it declines to on purpose. `no-overflow.spec.ts:43-45` records the decision in terms — 'ONE SCHEME for the wider bands, deliberately: horizontal overflow is box geometry and dark/light change no widths' — and 393 keeps both schemes 'because that is where content is tightest'. The e2e manifest confirms the shipped shape: `manifest.json` carries `393px no-overflow · dark scheme` AND `393px no-overflow · light scheme` entries, but `tablet 834 no-overflow · dark scheme` (`:604`) with no light-scheme counterpart at 834, 900 or 1280 (grepped this round: no `light scheme` title after the 393 block). So AC-78 and AC-24 as written are either (a) certified against a suite that never ran half of what they claim — the exact 'green suite that lies' pm's own risk 9 names — or (b) a silent doubling of the wide-band matrix that reverses a documented decision. The BRIEF carries the same error ('the no-overflow suite stays green at 393 / 834 / 900 / 1280 in both schemes'), and ux's UX-20 and UX-50 inherit it.
conflicts.proposal: Write the criterion to the suite's actual shape: both schemes at 393; one scheme at 834, 900 and 1280. If the owner wants light at the wide bands, that is a deliberate reversal of `no-overflow.spec.ts:43-45` and belongs in the build report as a change to the suite's design, with the widened matrix's runtime cost named. Either way the row must be provable with `npx playwright test --list` before GATE Q, not with a passing summary — `playwright.config.ts` is an explicit `testMatch` allowlist and an unregistered spec reports green by never running.

conflicts.quote: 834 added to the standing overflow suite — **phase 4**.
conflicts.why: Wrong on a checkable fact, and the same error appears in pm's Scope-Out ('the responsive sweep that adds 834 to the overflow suite — **phase 4**') and in the BRIEF ('the landing, the site pages and the responsive sweep that adds 834 to the overflow suite are phase 4'). 834 is ALREADY in the standing suite: `no-overflow.spec.ts:51` declares `{ label: 'tablet 834', width: 834, height: 1112 }` inside `WIDE_VIEWPORTS`, and `:48-50` records it as a v2 addition made against canon rule 17. `manifest.json:604` pins six shipped `tablet 834 no-overflow · dark scheme` cases (one per route). It shipped in phase 1. The BRIEF is wrong on this and so is the canon's phase assignment.
conflicts.proposal: Delete the future-dated row and the Scope-Out clause; replace both with the true obligation, which is smaller: 834 is already green and this phase must KEEP it green through the desk rebuild. Note the coupling my §6 flagged — `no-overflow.spec.ts:398` uses `page.getByText('Call wall').first()` as the readiness anchor for `/ticker/TSLA` at every width, and this phase deletes `DealerPositioning`, which renders that text today. The ladder keeps the exact label word (decisions §2: 'the side is in the label words'), so the anchor survives — but deliberately, not by luck. A rename reds ~12 e2e cases for a reason nobody will connect to a copy change.

conflicts.quote: Every non-mid row shows its distance from the mid; the mid row shows no distance.
conflicts.why: Unsatisfiable against shipped code without changing every number the trader has read for months, and self-contradictory with canon 14's own liveness clause. The shipped anchor is the levels spot, not the mid: `_kit/distanceToLevel.ts:11-14` (`levelSpot`) prefers `gex_spot` and falls back to `price`, and `DealerPositioning.tsx:61` uses exactly that. `copy.ts:318` labels `gex_spot` as 'levels spot' with the comment 'NOT spot — the levels anchor is not the live display price'. These are different numbers by construction: `gex_spot` is the last session close when the market is closed and live in RTH; `price` is the live/delayed display spot. Anchoring the column on the mid also makes all four structure rows recompute on every tick — five live rows — which canon 14 forbids in the same sentence that AC-16 is drawn from. ux reached the same conclusion independently at CI-9 and routed the canon wording as a product amendment; the AC text itself is a factual correction, not a preference.
conflicts.proposal: AC-16 becomes: every non-mid row shows its distance from the ladder's declared anchor (the levels spot, `gex_spot` else `price`), the ladder names that anchor once (pm's AC-17 already requires this), and the mid row's distance cell renders the not-applicable member rather than a computed zero — zero would assert the mid equals the structure anchor, which it usually does not. The canon rule 14 wording amendment is ux's product conflict and I do not re-raise it here.

conflicts.quote: With the operating system's reduce-motion setting on, the field drift, the tape trail and the mid beam render as static frames, and every value they carry is still readable as text.
conflicts.why: The first clause is right and cheap. The second clause silently prices a surface this phase's feasibility note does not contain, and only the owner can decide whether to buy it. The field carries the whole net-GEX-by-strike curve, the wall lines and the flip line, and it carries them ONLY as canvas pixels: `StructureFieldCanvas.tsx` has no `aria-`, no `role=` and no visually-hidden text anywhere in its directory (grepped this round, zero matches), and its only hook import is `useReducedMotion` at `:11`. 'Every value they carry is still readable as text' therefore means inventing a DOM text equivalent for a continuous curve over a spot ±20% strike grid — a new surface with its own copy, its own container-step behaviour and its own 44px questions. The BRIEF prices the hero as 'a re-housing of a shipped Canvas2D instrument, not a new chart'. The tape trail and the mid beam are different: their values already have DOM homes (the ladder's mid row and `LiveTape`'s cells), so the clause is already satisfied for them at zero cost. I am not proposing which way this goes — it is scope and user value, and the accessibility argument for buying it is genuinely strong.
conflicts.proposal: Split AC-12. Keep the static-frame clause at every width for all three motions, verified in the browser at both reduce-motion settings. Then the owner rules on the text clause: EITHER scope it to the tape trail and mid beam (true today, free) and book 'the structure field has no text equivalent' as named debt with a phase attached; OR put a text equivalent of the field in scope this phase and price it, in which case it needs its own criterion and its own surface. Related and in the same decision: `StructureFieldCanvas.tsx` imports no theme and fills `INK = '#0B0F17'` unconditionally at `:223` and `:434`, so promoting it to THE hero ships a dark rectangle inside a light desk unless light-mode parity is also ruled in or named.

conflicts.quote: All nine named states are independently reachable in a state harness, and **no two of them render the same primary line**.
conflicts.why: Self-revision. This is my count-shaped row and it is unsatisfiable against a correct implementation, exactly as ruling 3's row was. ux §2.4 establishes that A5 (stale) composes *over* a produced read and A9 (the drawer) opens *from* one; the architect independently reads the shipped machine as a `(requestState, resultState)` pair over 15 × 6, not a flat enum. So a stale trade read and a fresh trade read render the SAME verdict as their primary line — correctly, because stale is a strip over a still-legible read — and my row fails them both. Written as it stands, AC-38 makes GATE Q either FAIL correct code or force a build that replaces the read on staleness, which is the honesty regression the state exists to prevent. I withdraw the sentence rather than defend it.
conflicts.proposal: Split AC-38 into three rows, none asserting a count: (a) each of the nine named render cases is independently reachable from at least one producible input in the harness; (b) the seven exclusive body cases each render an observable marker that no other body case renders (non-synonymy, the AC-50 idiom, never a tally); (c) stale and the full-analysis drawer are asserted as COMPOSITION over a produced read — the read stays present and readable beneath/behind them — and never as replacements for it. Ship-blocking mark stays on (b) and (c). AC-63 (both widths) inherits the same three-part shape.

conflicts.quote: Every non-mid row shows its distance from the mid; the mid row shows no distance.
conflicts.why: Self-revision. I wrote the anchor from canon rule 14's wording without reading the shipped computation. Both other lanes read it at source and agree, and I verified it myself this round: `_kit/distanceToLevel.ts:11-14` anchors on `gex_spot ?? price`, not the mid, and `DealerPositioning.tsx:61` uses exactly that. Two consequences I did not price. First, my row silently changes every distance the trader has read for months. Second, anchoring on the live mid would make all four structure rows recompute on every tick — five live rows — which canon 14 forbids in the same sentence it states the anchor in. The second half of my row is also wrong in a smaller way: "shows no distance" is an empty cell in a column, which is the improvised absence `[absent-is-not-none]` names.
conflicts.proposal: Rewrite as: every non-mid row shows its distance from the levels anchor that AC-17 requires the ladder to name once; the mid row's distance cell renders a member of the closed not-a-number vocabulary rather than an empty cell or a computed zero. AC-17 already carries the naming property and needs no change. I also second ux's amendment request on canon rule 14's "distance from mid" wording rather than filing it a second time — it is one owner call, raised by ux, and I do not need it duplicated in the queue.

conflicts.quote: 834 added to the standing overflow suite — **phase 4**.
conflicts.why: Self-revision. False, and I verified the architect's correction at source this round: `apps/dashboard-e2e/src/e2e/no-overflow.spec.ts:51` already contains `{ label: 'tablet 834', width: 834, height: 1112 }` inside `WIDE_VIEWPORTS`, and line 962 walks that list. 834 shipped in phase 1. Future-dating shipped work is not a harmless tidiness error: it makes this phase look smaller than it is, and it gives a build lane a written permission slip to treat an 834 failure as "phase 4's job" when the suite is already red on it. My Scope-Out row carries the same mistake in the same words.
conflicts.proposal: Delete the Future-dated row and the '(The 834 width is still *checked* here; adding it to the standing suite is phase 4's job.)' clause from Scope-Out. AC-24 and AC-78 already assert 393 / 834 / 900 / 1280 and are now assertions against a suite that runs all four today, which makes them cheaper, not more expensive. Nothing else in my set moves.

conflicts.quote: Alerts is a phase-3 surface and canon rule 19 lists it as a nav destination, not a shipped capability.
conflicts.why: Self-revision, and it changes the answer to the question I raised. The second half of that sentence is false. `apps/dashboard/src/app/pages/alerts/AlertsPage.tsx:24` ships a `level_touch` alert kind, `:27-31` ship a level reference list including `gamma_flip`, `call_wall`, `put_wall` and a `price` threshold, `:42-49` compose a rule, and `features/alerts/store.ts:44` persists it to the already-existing durable key `convexa.alerts.v1` (`types.ts:47`). So alerting on a level is a shipped capability, reachable from a hook, with no backend change and no NEW durable key — which is the thing the architect's non-goal 7 actually fences. Plainly, then: a dead control does NOT have to ship, and I withdraw the framing that the only choices were a decorative button or a different action. What is left is a scope call, not a feasibility one. This BRIEF says alerts keeps its current composition in phase 3, and wiring the desk's no-trade state into `addRule` adds a new entry point to a phase-3 surface — small, but it is scope, and I will not take it silently. (Housekeeping: my Scope-Out row cites AC-40 for this guard; the row is AC-45.)
conflicts.proposal: Owner call, two options, both honest. (a) Phase 2 wires the no-trade state's primary action into the shipped alert store — the state ends in something that works end to end, the desk gains one entry point, and the alerts page's composition is untouched. (b) The no-trade state ends in an action this build already performs on that panel (Refresh, or Full analysis — both are drawn in the same stack at `design/src/screens/ai-read.mjs:89`), and the alert entry point waits for phase 3 with the rest of the alerts work. AC-45 is unchanged under either and is the row that forces the choice into the open instead of letting a decorative button land.

conflicts.quote: | UX-30 | The verdict word is the first content node in the panel's reading order and is the panel's only amber spend | A3·A4 | **test** | DOM order and a colour census both regress silently |
conflicts.why: ux scopes the only-amber assertion to A3 and A4 — the two produced states. My AC-31 scopes it to the panel in every state. The gap is not academic: in loading, idle, add-a-key and signed-out there is no verdict word at all, so under ux's scope the panel may spend amber with nothing to justify it, and under mine it may spend none anywhere. The drawn source spends amber inside the panel four times — `design/src/screens/ai-read.mjs:8` (header icon tint), `:15` (the pinned-read provenance dot), `:67` (the `Thinking…` pulse) and `:71` (the model spinner's top edge) — and I verified all four this round. What decides the kind is `:140`: the same file draws a legend chip reading `amber spent once` beside those four spends. The author believed rule 16 held while spending amber four more times, which means "spend" is genuinely ambiguous between 'any amber pixel in the panel' and 'the display-type word'. That ambiguity is not a fact two lanes can settle by reading a file — it is what the rule is for, and only the owner sets it. I also withdraw the conditional hedge inside AC-31 itself ('if the ruling narrows the rule, this row narrows to...'): a criterion that branches on a pending ruling is not checkable as written, which is my own defining failure mode.
conflicts.proposal: Owner call on rule 16's scope, then one unconditional criterion. If the rule is literal, AC-31 stands panel-wide in every state, the four drawn spends are defects to regenerate out of `design/`, and ux adds the ai-read amber to its §6 amendment 3 list (it currently names figure-cell, ladder, desk and desk-states, not ai-read). If the owner rules that amber outside the verdict is intended, rule 16 takes a one-clause amendment naming exactly where — icon tint, provenance dot, in-flight pulse — and AC-31 narrows to 'the verdict word is the only amber-rendered TEXT in the panel, in every state', with a colour census asserting the amendment's list is closed. Either way one criterion, no branch, and the same observable in produced and non-produced states.

conflicts.quote: | UX-32 | `no_trade` renders with no warning chrome, no error tone, the same typographic weight as a trade, and a useful primary action | A4 | **test** | It is a correct answer being mistaken for a failure — the exact silent misread |
conflicts.why: Three quarters of this row is exactly right and I adopt it. The last clause is not observable: 'a useful primary action' is an intention, and a reviewer looking at a button labelled `Alert me at 575` will read it as useful whether or not pressing it does anything. It is marked `test`, and no test can assert usefulness — so the row would ship as a green assertion over the three checkable clauses while the unverifiable one carries the honesty. This is the exact failure shape I am supposed to catch in my own rows, and it is worth more caught in a peer's than defended in mine.
conflicts.proposal: Replace the last clause with the observable: '...and the primary action it offers is one this build performs end to end.' That keeps ux's state mapping and its `test` mark intact (the first three clauses are the testable ones and stay), and it makes the fourth checkable by a stranger who presses the button. It is also the same property my AC-45 asserts, so the two rows converge rather than compete.

conflicts.quote: The strip renders eight cells at every state; an unavailable metric is an `unavailable` cell, not a missing one.
conflicts.why: This is right in general and wrong for the eighth cell, and my AC-26 makes the same mistake in the same direction — so I am withdrawing my row's coverage of off-exchange in the same breath. ux CI-6 verified against PROJECT_CONTEXT §5 that the off-exchange object is omitted BOTH when `INCLUDE_DARK_POOL=false` and when the best-effort computation fails, and both arrive at the frontend as the same absent object. With the `apps/api` diff required to be empty this phase, the frontend cannot tell 'we did not look' from 'we looked and failed'. `unavailable` asserts a cycle that ran and produced nothing — a claim the app cannot observe. So the architect's rule, applied to that cell, fabricates a cause; ux's answer (cell absent) recreates `[absent-is-not-none]` in the scroll axis, because at 393px a cell that is not there is indistinguishable from a cell that scrolled off the rail — which is ux's own risk 5. Both lanes are right about the other's failure and neither has proposed the render that is true under both causes.
conflicts.proposal: Keep the architect's structural rule — eight fixed slots at every state, no reflow, which is what AC-26 and ux's S4 both need — and let the off-exchange slot render the vocabulary member whose meaning is 'the feed did not send it', which is true whether the flag disabled it or the computation failed and asserts nothing about which. Ruling 3 settles that the caller picks the member and the type enforces only closure, so this needs no tenth member and no new copy branch. The 'attempted vs failed' wire discriminator is booked as named debt with a phase attached, per ux CI-6. My AC-26 is rewritten to require the member the app can honestly claim rather than a specific literal.

conflicts.quote: | A1 | idle | body | A2–A4, A6–A8 | "Ready to read this snapshot." + the composer |
conflicts.why: The marker this row keys on cannot tell two shipped states apart. The architect read `presentationPolicy.ts:20-26` and found four result states with no canon home, one of which is `no_edge`; `presentationPolicy.ts:168` already ships an `askAnyway` action for it, and `design/src/screens/ai-read.mjs:62` draws it as a footnote inside the idle panel. A panel showing 'Ready to read this snapshot' plus the composer renders identically for plain idle and for idle-with-a-quiet-gate-note under this marker, so UX-28 ('each renders its own marker') would pass while certifying precisely the collapse it exists to prevent. My own AC-39 has the same hole — it enumerates idle's contents and never mentions the gate note. Answering the question put to me directly: my R1 risk 2 ('there is no failure state among the nine') and the architect's 15 × 6 finding are NOT the same finding. The architect's is strictly larger and strictly better evidenced — it names four homeless shipped states where I named one missing canon slot — and it corrects my framing: `unavailable` is not a state that must be invented, it already ships with its own copy at `ai-rec/copy.ts:51-52`, and ux confirms a rate limit must never wear it. My AC-57 stays as written because it asserts a producible observable, but it covers one of the four, not the class. I raise this as the criterion-shape defect only: the architect has already routed the disposition of `no_edge`, `unavailable`, `superseded_inputs` and `incomplete_trade` to the owner, I agree with that routing, and duplicating it would spend the owner's attention twice on one question.
conflicts.proposal: Idle carries two observable arms in the AC-38(b) non-synonymy set: plain idle, and idle-with-the-gate-note whose marker is the note plus the ask-anyway control. Neither is permitted to render the other's marker. The three remaining homeless states get their AC rows once the owner rules where they land; until then no criterion may key idle, no-trade or add-a-key on a marker that any of them also renders.

conflicts.quote: **Structure-field hero** — field, ladder, tape trail and structure path in one framed panel.
conflicts.why: Self-revision by omission. My Scope-In row and my Scope-Out list are both silent on colour-scheme parity for the hero's canvas, and silence is not available here. The architect read `StructureFieldCanvas.tsx` at source: it imports no theme (`:11`), declares module-level hex literals (`:20-27`) and fills its background with the dark `INK` literal unconditionally (`:223`, `:434`), with no `palette.mode` branch in 887 lines. Today that is one widget among thirteen. This phase promotes it to THE hero, so in light mode the desk's central instrument is a dark rectangle inside a light panel. None of my rows catch it — AC-78's both-schemes check is about horizontal overflow, and a dark hero overflows nothing. The architect flagged this as a product call and made it a falsifiable assumption about me; I omitted it, so the assumption was falsified and the honest repair is to route it rather than quietly absorb it into a lane's judgement.
